body:
## Summary
- Adds `BeadCloser` interface and queue expiry tracking to the reconciler
- Beads deferred due to max pods/burst limit/rate limit are tracked in a `deferredSince` map across reconcile passes
- When a bead exceeds `CoopQueueExpiryTimeout` (default: 1h, env: `COOP_QUEUE_EXPIRY_TIMEOUT`), it is auto-closed with `agent_state=expired` and a `close_reason` field
- Setting `COOP_QUEUE_EXPIRY_TIMEOUT=0` disables expiry (beads queue indefinitely)
- Tracking is cleaned up when beads get pods or are removed from desired state

## Changed files
- `config/config.go` — `CoopQueueExpiryTimeout` field + env parsing
- `reconciler/reconciler.go` — `BeadCloser` interface, `SetBeadCloser()`, `deferredSince` map, `expireDeferredBeads()`, deferral tracking at 4 callsites
- `reconciler/reconciler_test.go` — 4 new tests
- `cmd/controller/main.go` — `rec.SetBeadCloser(daemon)` wiring

## Test plan
- [x] `TestReconcile_QueueExpiry_ClosesExpiredBeads` — verifies auto-close after timeout
- [x] `TestReconcile_QueueExpiry_ClearsTrackingWhenPodCreated` — verifies cleanup when pods are created
- [x] `TestReconcile_QueueExpiry_DisabledWhenZeroTimeout` — verifies no expiry when disabled
- [x] `TestReconcile_QueueExpiry_NilCloserDoesNotPanic` — verifies safety with nil closer
- [x] Full `go test ./...` passes (28 packages)

useRecipeCache.js (new):
- TTL-based localStorage cache (1h default, configurable)
- getCached(key): returns data if not expired, cleans stale entry
- setCache(key, data): saves with timestamp, prunes expired entries
- clearAll(): wipe cooking cache (useful for settings page)

useBottomSheet.js (new):
- mount/visible two-phase state for proper enter+exit animations
- Enter: translateY 100%→0 (280ms cubic-bezier ease-out)
- Exit: translateY 0→100% (280ms), then unmount after timer
- handleProps: touchStart/Move/End for drag handle only (no passive issues)
- Swipe detection: close if dragY > 90px or velocity > 0.45 px/ms
- Snap back: dragY resets to 0 with CSS transition on release

RecipeBottomSheet.jsx (new):
- Mobile: 90dvh sheet, animated enter/exit, swipe handle, X button
- Desktop: centered modal with scale+opacity animation
- Syncs to recipe prop via useEffect → open/close the hook
- Body scroll lock while mounted

useCooking.js:
- Replaced manual readStoredJson/writeStoredJson cache with useRecipeCache
- TTL hit → returns cached data without API call
- In-flight deduplication still active via activeKeys Set

CookingHome.jsx:
- getRecommendedIndex(): picks best recipe per tipo+mode signals (proteico→max protein, liviano/snack→min cal, cookNow→fastest, mealPrep/default→"balanceada" label)

## Summary
- Adds a stale agent reaper that periodically checks agent bead `updated_at` timestamps and terminates pods that haven't reported activity within a configurable window (default: 2 hours)
- Closes stale beads (sets `agent_state` to `failed`) and deletes their K8s pods to free pod slots
- Only reaps agents in "working" state — skips spawning, prewarmed, and terminal states
- Configurable via `STALE_AGENT_TIMEOUT` env var (default: `2h`, set to `0` to disable)

## Changes
- `internal/statusreporter/stalereaper.go` — New `StaleReaper` struct with `Reap()` method
- `internal/statusreporter/stalereaper_test.go` — Tests for reaping logic, state filtering, error handling
- `internal/beadsapi/client.go` — Added `UpdatedAt` field to `AgentBead` struct
- `internal/config/config.go` — Added `StaleAgentTimeout` config field
- `cmd/controller/main.go` — Wire stale reaper into periodic sync loop (runs every 5 min)

## Test plan

- [x] Both controller and slack-bridge binaries build
- [x] New stale reaper tests cover: reaping working agents past timeout, skipping non-working states, skipping zero updated_at, continuing on close errors, disabled when timeout is 0

author: shiba4life
body:
## Summary

- Wires `SyncEngine::bootstrap()` into `POST /api/auth/restore` so recovering from a 24-word BIP39 phrase also restores the full database from Cloudflare R2, not just the Ed25519 identity keys
- After `signed_register` succeeds and returns `api_key` credentials, a background task creates a temporary `SyncEngine`, downloads the latest snapshot, and replays any write logs
- Bootstrap runs asynchronously so the restore endpoint returns immediately — if bootstrap fails, the error is logged but restore still succeeds (identity was already restored)

## Implementation

The new `bootstrap_from_cloud()` helper follows the same pattern as `migrate_to_cloud()` in `admin_ops.rs`:
1. Loads E2E encryption keys from `$FOLDDB_HOME/e2e.key`
2. Resolves the Sled storage path from `NodeConfig`
3. Builds a `SyncSetup` + `SyncEngine` with the Exemem credentials
4. Opens the local Sled DB as a `NamespacedStore`
5. Calls `engine.bootstrap()` to download snapshot + replay logs

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` passes (confirmed locally)
- [ ] Verify `cargo check --workspace --features aws-backend` passes (confirmed locally)
- [ ] Verify `cargo test --workspace --all-targets` passes (one pre-existing test failure on main, unrelated)
- [ ] Manual test: restore from phrase on a fresh node with existing cloud data → database should be populated after restore

body: **What is this feature?** This PR adds explicit error handling with user-visible error messages and retry functionality to dashboard feature API calls that previously had missing or weak error handling. Users now see clear error alerts with retry buttons instead of silent failures or confusing empty states. **Why do we need this feature?** Several dashboard feature components had API calls that either: - Silently caught errors and returned empty data (making failures indistinguishable from "no results") - Left spinners stuck indefinitely on network failures - Had no user-facing error messages or recovery options This caused poor UX when API calls failed—users couldn't tell if something went wrong or how to recover. **Who is this feature for?** All Grafana users who interact with dashboard library features, template dashboards, suggested dashboards, snapshot sharing, and version history. **Which issue(s) does this PR fix?** Fixes missing error handling in dashboard API calls. **Special notes for your reviewer:** ## Changes made ### Dashboard Library components - `TemplateDashboardModal.tsx`: Added error state UI with Alert and Retry button using `useAsyncRetry` - `SuggestedDashboards.tsx`: Added error handling for mixed provisioned/community dashboard fetching - `DashboardLibrarySection.tsx`: Added error UI for provisioned dashboard loading - `BasicProvisionedDashboardsEmptyPage.tsx`: Added error state display with retry ### Snapshot/Share workflows - `ShareSnapshot.tsx` (classic): Added try/catch with error alerts for snapshot create/delete operations - `ShareSnapshotTab.tsx` (scene): Added error handling for sharing options load and snapshot operations ### Version History - `VersionsEditView.tsx`: Fixed spinner-stuck-on-error behavior, added error UI for version list and diff loading - `RevertDashboardModal.tsx`: Added error alert display when dashboard restore fails ### Tests added - `TemplateDashboardModal.test.tsx`: Tests for error alert display and retry behavior - `DashboardLibrarySection.test.tsx`: Tests for error handling and retry functionality - `SuggestedDashboards.test.tsx`: Tests for error state and retry action Please check that: - [x] It works as expected from a user's perspective. - [x] If this is a pre-GA feature, it is behind a feature toggle. - [ ] The docs are updated, and if this is a [notable improvement](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/#how-to-determine-if-content-belongs-in-whats-new), it's added to our [What's New](https://grafana.com/docs/writers-toolkit/contribute/release-notes/) doc.

Adds a standalone `money-manager.html` page to the site — a localStorage-backed personal finance tracker for manually entering recurring bills/subscriptions and paydays, with a live dashboard overview.

## New files

- **`money-manager.html`** — App shell with an Overview dashboard (monthly totals, net cash flow, next payday, upcoming-this-month list) and two tabbed panels: Bills & Subscriptions and Paydays
- **`css/money-manager.css`** — Page-specific styles using the existing design tokens (`--beige`, `--navy`, card/chip/button patterns)

- **Bills & Subscriptions** — add/edit/delete entries with name, amount, due day-of-month, category (9 types with emoji icons), and optional notes
- **Paydays** — add/edit/delete with label, amount, frequency (monthly / bi-weekly / weekly), and next occurrence date; future dates auto-rolled forward
- **Dashboard** — monthly income normalised across frequencies (`weekly × 4.333`, `biweekly × 2.167`), net cash flow, next payday, and a sorted upcoming-this-month list colour-coded by type
- All user data rendered exclusively via `textContent`/DOM APIs — no `innerHTML` with user-supplied values

author: copilot
body:
Faculty files lacked visibility controls (all files visible to the faculty member) and allowed Register Office staff to delete files directly without oversight.

## Schema (`admin/faculty-files-v2.sql`)
- `faculty_files.is_internal` — when set, file is hidden from the owning faculty member; visible only to the uploader, Register Office, and super admins
- `faculty_file_delete_requests` — tracks pending/approved/rejected delete requests with requester, reviewer, notes, and a snapshot of file metadata for cleanup

## Access control (`fp-helpers.php`)
- `fp_can_view_file(array $file)` — gates visibility; internal files pass only for super admin, Register Office, or the original uploader
- `fp_can_request_delete()` — replaces direct-delete gate; Register Office can request, super admins bypass the queue

## Upload form (`files.php`)
- Added **Internal only** checkbox; saves `is_internal` on INSERT
- File list filtered through `fp_can_view_file()` at fetch time — faculty never receive internal file rows
- Internal files show a lock badge to staff
- Register Office sees a **Request Delete** button → modal with optional reason; row shows **⏳ Pending Deletion** badge once submitted
- Super admin header button shows pending request count badge

## Delete handler (`file-delete.php`)
- Super admin → immediate delete (unchanged behaviour)
- Register Office → inserts into `faculty_file_delete_requests`; guards against duplicate pending requests for the same file

## Review page (`pending-deletes.php`) — new, super admin only
- Lists requests filterable by status (pending / approved / rejected / all)
- **Approve** executes physical + DB deletion; **Reject** preserves the file; both record a reviewer note and log the action via `log_change()`

body:
## Summary

- The synchronous `ignore::WalkBuilder` walk in `index_project` ran on a tokio worker thread, blocking it for the duration of directory traversal. On repos with many files this starved the TUI render loop (250 ms tick), preventing the interface from appearing until indexing finished.
- Directory walk and `current_files` HashSet construction are now wrapped in `tokio::task::spawn_blocking`. `JoinError` (closure panic) is mapped to `IndexError::Other`.

- TUI starts and renders immediately; indexing progress updates continue via the existing `IndexProgress` watch channel.

body:
## What changed                                                                                                                                                     
  - New `LIND_DYLINK=1` codepath in `compile_coreutils.sh`:                                                                                                           
    - Adds `-fPIC` to `CFLAGS_WASM`.                                                                                                                                  
    - Switches `LDFLAGS_WASM` to the dylink set: `-nostartfiles`, `-Wl,-pie`, `--import-table`, `--shared-memory`, `--allow-undefined`,                               
  `--unresolved-symbols=import-dynamic`, and the required exports (`__wasm_call_ctors`, `__wasm_init_tls`, `__tls_base`).                                             
    - Links in three dylink CRT objects: `set_stack_pointer.o`, `crt1_shared.o`, `lind_utils.o`. The script aborts with an actionable hint if any are missing.        
    - Runs each `.wasm` through `add-export-tool` to export `__wasm_apply_tls_relocs`, `__wasm_apply_global_relocs`, `__stack_pointer` — required by the lind-boot    
  dynamic loader.                                                                                                                                                     
    - Uses dylink-specific `wasm-opt` flags: `--enable-bulk-memory --enable-threads --epoch-injection --pass-arg=epoch-import --pass-arg=epoch-main-module --asyncify 
  --pass-arg=asyncify-import-globals`.                                                                                                                                
  - `$LIND_DYLINK` is part of the configure signature, so flipping modes triggers a reconfigure.  

 ## Dependencies                                                                                                                                                     
 Requires a companion change in **lind-wasm** adding `./intl/Versions` and `./iconv/Versions` to `scripts/version-path-minimal.txt`, without which ~10 coreutils   tools fail to load with `unknown import: env::bindtextdomain` or `env::iconv_open`. See lind-wasm PR #TBD.

body: ## Summary When AI reformats code (reflow/reformatting), the resulting lines were sometimes incorrectly attributed to human instead of AI. This PR fixes attribution for both reflow directions in the attribution tracker, and adds regression tests confirming human reflows don't steal AI attribution. All changes are scoped to `attribution_tracker.rs` (core logic) and the new test file. ### Two fixes in `attribution_tracker.rs` **1. N→1 reflow by AI** When AI merges multiple lines into one, the token-aligned sub-hunk diffing was preserving matching tokens with their original (human) author. Fix: expand the force-split condition to include the N→1 case (`new_line_count == 1`), emitting Delete+Insert ops so `transform_attributions` assigns AI to all new bytes. **2. 1→N reflow by AI** When AI splits one line into multiple, we need to force-split the hunk — but naively doing so also catches cases where AI *appends* new lines after a human line (the trailing `\n` pulls the human line into the changed hunk). Fix: add `is_whitespace_only_change()` helper that compares non-whitespace content of old vs new. Only force-split 1→N hunks when the non-whitespace content is identical (a pure reflow). ### Tests 8 new regression tests (4 scenarios × 2 worktree variants), all passing, zero ignored: - `test_ai_reflow_two_lines_to_one_attributed_to_ai` — original bug report scenario (N→1) - `test_ai_reflow_of_human_content_one_to_many_lines_attributed_to_ai` — 1→N inverse - `test_human_reflow_on_ai_code_retains_ai_attribution` — human reflows AI code intra-commit (AI checkpoint → human checkpoint → commit), verifies AI attribution is retained - `test_human_reflow_of_ai_set_contents_retains_ai` — Chinese text + set_contents flow, intra-commit Human reflow tests operate intra-commit (AI checkpoint then human checkpoint in the same session, no commit between them) so the working log retains AI attributions and the attribution tracker handles the reflow purely through its own logic. ## Review & Testing Checklist for Human - [ ] **Verify operator precedence in the force-split condition** (`attribution_tracker.rs`): The condition is `(new_line_count == 1 || old_line_count == new_line_count) && old_line_count > 1 || is_one_to_many_reflow`. Confirm this evaluates as intended: `((new==1 || old==new) && old>1) || is_one_to_many_reflow`. - [ ] **Review the `is_whitespace_only_change` heuristic**: It strips all whitespace and compares. A reflow that *also* changes a token (e.g. AI reflows AND fixes a typo) will NOT be detected as a reflow and will fall back to the token-aligned path. Confirm this conservative behavior is acceptable. - [ ] **Spot-check with a real AI-generated commit**: Run `git-ai` against a real commit that includes a reflow and verify end-to-end. **Suggested test plan:** Apply a formatter (e.g. `rustfmt`) to a file with mixed human/AI attribution and run a checkpoint. Verify AI lines retain AI attribution and human lines retain human attribution. ### Notes - All changes are in `attribution_tracker.rs` only — no checkpoint.rs modifications. - The `is_whitespace_only_change` check is intentionally conservative — if in doubt, it falls back to the existing token-aligned path rather than risk misattribution. - Cross-commit human reflow (formatter runs in a separate session after an AI commit) is not covered by these tests. That scenario hits the checkpoint fast-path which returns empty attributions; fixing it would require checkpoint.rs changes that are out of scope for this PR. - All tests use raw `fs::write` + `checkpoint` to replicate the exact real-world flow per original request. Link to Devin session: https://app.devin.ai/sessions/59473e4150df41c8a1cfaa9d43fbd61b Requested by: @svarlamov ---

## Summary

- Adds an optional cross-platform GUI splash screen that displays during PyApp's first-run bootstrap and `self restore`, showing a logo, progress bar, and status messages
- Gated behind a `splash` Cargo feature flag — zero overhead when disabled, binary identical to upstream
- Uses `eframe`/`egui` (OpenGL/glow renderer) for cross-platform windowing (Windows, macOS, Linux)
- Supports dark/light themes, customisable colours, and embedded PNG/JPEG logo images
- All configuration via `PYAPP_SPLASH_*` environment variables at build time, following PyApp's established pattern

## Configuration

| Variable | Default | Description |
|----------|---------|-------------|
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_ENABLED` | `false` | Set to `true` + build with `--features splash` |
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_THEME` | `dark` | `dark` or `light` |
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_IMAGE` | None | Path to PNG/JPEG logo file |
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_BG_COLOR` | Theme default | Background colour (hex) |
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_TEXT_COLOR` | Theme default | Text colour (hex) |
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_PROGRESS_COLOR` | Theme default | Progress bar colour (hex) |
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_WINDOW_TITLE` | `PYAPP_PROJECT_NAME` | Window title |
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_WINDOW_WIDTH` | `480` | Window width (px) |
| `PYAPP_SPLASH_WINDOW_HEIGHT` | `360` | Window height (px) |

## Architecture

- `src/splash/` module with `config.rs`, `progress.rs`, `window.rs`, `mod.rs`
- Splash runs on main thread (required by macOS), bootstrap work on background thread
- Communication via `std::sync::mpsc` channels
- Graceful degradation: if window creation fails, bootstrap proceeds silently
- Version: `v0.29.0-splash.1`

## Test plan

- [ ] Build with splash + dark theme + no logo — text fallback displayed
- [ ] Build with splash + dark theme + logo image — logo displayed
- [ ] Build with splash + light theme — correct light colours

body:
# Add support for skill dependencies via frontmatter `depends` field

Fixes #860

## Summary

Implements automatic dependency resolution for skills, allowing skills to declare dependencies in their frontmatter that are automatically installed in the correct order.

## Root Cause

Skills could reference sibling skills via relative paths (e.g., `Read ../gws-shared/SKILL.md`), but `npx skills add` had no awareness of these references. When users selectively installed a single skill, prerequisite skills were silently missing, leaving broken references.

## Changes

- Added `depends?: string[]` field to `Skill` interface in `src/types.ts`
- Updated `parseSkillMd()` to parse and validate `depends` field from frontmatter
- Implemented `resolveDependencies()` function with:
  - Recursive dependency resolution (A → B → C installs all three)
  - Circular dependency detection with clear error messages
  - Missing dependency detection with helpful error messages
- Implemented `formatDependencyTree()` to display dependency relationships to users
- Integrated dependency resolution into installation flow in `src/add.ts`:
  - Resolves dependencies before installation
  - Installs in correct order (dependencies first)
  - Displays dependency tree for skills with dependencies
  - Handles errors gracefully with clear messages
- Added comprehensive test coverage:
  - Unit tests for dependency resolution and cycle detection
  - Integration tests for skill discovery with dependencies
- Updated documentation:
  - Added `depends` field documentation to README.md
  - Updated skill template in `src/cli.ts` with commented example

## Why This Is Safe

- Dependencies are only resolved from the same repository (security constraint)
- Existing skills without dependencies continue to work unchanged
- Invalid `depends` values (non-array, non-string elements) are logged as warnings but don't break installation
- Circular dependencies are detected and fail with clear error messages
- Missing dependencies fail with actionable error messages

## Testing

**Unit Tests (7 tests):**
- ✅ Detects circular dependencies
- ✅ Resolves linear dependencies (A → B → C)
- ✅ Handles shared dependencies (A → C, B → C installs C once)
- ✅ Throws error when dependency not found
- ✅ Handles skills with no dependencies
- ✅ Formats simple dependency tree
- ✅ Formats nested dependency tree

**Integration Tests (2 tests):**
- ✅ Discovers skills with dependencies from filesystem
- ✅ Handles nested dependencies (A → B → C)

**All tests pass:** 36/36 tests passing in `src/skills.test.ts` and `src/add.test.ts`

## Example Usage

**Skill with dependencies:**
```yaml
---
name: gws-drive
description: "Google Drive: Manage files, folders, and shared drives."
depends:
  - gws-shared
---
```

**Installation output:**
```
Dependency tree:
gws-drive
└─ gws-shared

Installing skills...
✓ gws-shared installed
✓ gws-drive installed
```

## Related

- Issue: #860
- Proposal: Add optional `depends` field to SKILL.md frontmatter spec
- Analogous to: `peerDependencies` in package managers

body:
## Summary

Implements relay roadmap items **E1**, **E2**, and **E3**.

### E1 - Semantic hook types
Three new named hook types that improve API discoverability over the generic `OnBeforeRequest`/`OnAfterResponse`:

| Option | Trigger | Use case |
|---|---|---|
| `WithBeforeRetryHook` | Before each retry sleep | Structured retry logging, metrics |
| `WithBeforeRedirectHook` | Before each redirect is followed | Audit redirect chains, abort on policy |
| `WithOnErrorHook` | When `Execute` returns non-nil error | Error metrics, alerting |

Hooks are composable - multiple calls append in registration order.  
`BeforeRetryHook` receives `ctx` + `*Request` unlike the lower-level `WithOnRetry`.  
Implementation uses a thread-safe per-Execute retrier copy (no global mutation).

### E2 - Auto idempotency on safe retries
`WithAutoIdempotencyOnSafeRetries()` injects `X-Idempotency-Key` only for RFC 9110 safe/idempotent methods (GET, HEAD, PUT, OPTIONS, TRACE). POST, PATCH, DELETE are skipped unless the caller sets a key explicitly. The existing `WithAutoIdempotencyKey()` is unchanged.

### E3 - Error classification helpers
Three new convenience predicates in `classification.go`:
- `IsRetryableError(err, resp)` - true for transient or rate-limited errors
- `IsTimeout(err)` - true for `ErrTimeout` or `context.DeadlineExceeded`
- `IsCircuitOpen(err)` - true for `ErrCircuitOpen`

## Tests
12 new tests in `hooks_test.go` - all passing. Full suite green.

author: copilot
body:
`PYTHON_BIN` is set by the `resolve-conda-isis-prefix` composite action, but when that action fails (e.g., missing `normalized-safe-checkout`) the variable is never exported. Any subsequent step using `set -u` then crashes immediately with `unbound variable` instead of surfacing the real error.

## Changes

- **All three workflows** (`reusable-pybind-build-github-hosted.yml`, `reusable-pybind-build-self-hosted.yml`, `ci-pybind.yml`): add a local fallback at the top of every step that invokes Python:

```bash
python_bin="${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}"
```

then replace `"$PYTHON_BIN"` with `"$python_bin"` throughout that step. Affected steps per workflow:

| Step | github-hosted | self-hosted | ci-pybind |
|---|---|---|---|
| Verify local toolchain | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Configure CMake | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ (rebuild step) |
| Summarize build failure | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Run smoke_import.py | ✓ | ✓ | — |
| Inventory / reporting steps | — | — | ✓ (3 steps) |

When `PYTHON_BIN` is set, its value is used as before. When it is absent, the step falls back to `python3` and continues rather than aborting with an unrelated unbound-variable error.

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

修复仓库 `gengxun-henu/pyisis` 中 GitHub Actions 工作流的 `PYTHON_BIN: unbound variable` 失败问题。

背景：
- 失败出现在 workflow run `23990455406` 的 job `69969190730`。
- 日志显示在构建失败汇总步骤中执行：
  - `"$PYTHON_BIN" scripts/build_log_analyzer.py "$BUILD_DIR/build.log"`
- 由于 `PYTHON_BIN` 未定义且 shell 使用 `set -u`，步骤直接失败：`line 2: PYTHON_BIN: unbound variable`。
- 相关工作流文件：
  - `.github/workflows/reusable-pybind-build-github-hosted.yml`
  - `.github/workflows/reusable-pybind-build-self-hosted.yml`
- 这些文件中多个步骤直接使用 `$PYTHON_BIN`，但当前流程未保证该变量始终被导出。

目标：
1. 修复 workflow，使其在 `PYTHON_BIN` 未显式设置时仍能稳定运行。
2. 优先采用低风险、可维护方案：在使用 Python 的 shell 步骤中提供合理回退，例如优先使用 `${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}`，必要时可进一步增强为检测 `python3`/`python`。
3. 至少修复以下位置：
   - `Summarize build failure`
   - 以及同文件中其它直接依赖 `$PYTHON_BIN` 的步骤，避免后续同类故障。
4. 保持现有工作流语义不变，不要引入破坏性重构。
5. 如有合适方式，可提炼为每个 step 内局部变量 `python_bin="${PYTHON_BIN:-python3}"` 后统一使用。

验收标准：
- 当 `PYTHON_BIN` 已设置时，仍优先使用其值。
- 当 `PYTHON_BIN` 未设置时，workflow 不应因 unbound variable 失败。
- github-hosted 与 self-hosted 两套 reusable workflow 都应覆盖。
- 修改应尽量小且清晰。

The following is the prior conversation context from the user's chat exploration (may be truncated):

User: Please find a solution for this failing job. Use the logs, job definition, and any referenced files where the failure occurred. Keep your response focused on the solution and include code suggestions when appropriate.

Assistant: The failure is caused by a missing local composite action, which then leaves `PYTHON_BIN` unset and causes the shell step to crash.

### Root cause
In the failing job log:

- `Can't find 'action.yml', 'action.yaml' or 'Dockerfile' under '/home/runner/work/pyisis/pyisis/.github/actions/normalized-safe-checkout'`
- then:
  - `/...sh: line 2: PYTHON_BIN: unbound variable`

That means the workflow tries to use this local action:

- `.github/workflows/ci-pybind.yml` at `6cd1df9e491dc3d9e6d38aeb2439b390985c94c1`, lines 71–77
- and similarly elsewhere in the workflow

```yaml
- name: Normalize and verify checkout transport
  uses: ./.github/actions/normalized-safe-checkout
```

But the referenced path does not contain a valid local action definition (`action.yml` / `action.yaml` / `Dockerfile`) at that commit.

### Fix
Make `.github/actions/normalized-safe-checkout` a valid composite action directory by adding an `action.yml` file there, or fix the workflow path if the action lives somewhere else.

A minimal `action.yml` should look like this:

```yaml
name: normalized-safe-checkout
description: Normalize repository checkout state and optionally run checkout

inputs:
  skip-checkout:
    description: Skip running actions/checkout because checkout already happened
    required: false
    default: "false"
  runner-mode:
    description: Runner mode
    required: false
    default: github-hosted
  github-token:
    description: GitHub token for checkout if needed
    required: false
    default: ""
  summary-context:
    description: Context label for step summary
    required: false
    default: ""

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Validate checkout exists
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        git rev-parse --show-toplevel
        git status --short >/dev/null
```

If the action is supposed to perform checkout when `skip-checkout` is false, expand it like this:

```yaml
name: normalized-safe-checkout
description: Normalize repository checkout state and optionally run checkout

inputs:
  skip-checkout:
    required: false
    default: "false"
  github-token:
    required: false
    default: ""
  runner-mode:
    required: false
    default: github-hosted
  summary-context:
    required: false
    default: ""

runs:
  using: composite
  steps:
    - name: Checkout repository when needed
      if: ${{ inputs.skip-checkout != 'true' }}
      uses: actions/checkout@v4
      with:
        token: ${{ inputs.github-token }}
        fetch-depth: 0

    - name: Normalize checkout
      shell: bash
      run: |
        set -euo pipefail
        git config --global --add safe.directory "$GITHUB_WORKSPACE"
        git rev-parse HEAD
```

### Why `PYTHON_BIN` failed next
The workflow later runs:

- `.github/workflows/ci-pybind.yml` lines 95–100

```yaml
- name: Ensure inventory summary exists
  run: |
    set -euo pipefail
    if [ ! -f class_bind_methods_details/methods_inventory_summary.csv ]; then
      "$PYTHON_BIN" class_bind_methods_details/generate_methods_csv.py
    fi
```

`PYTHON_BIN` is expected to be populated by an earlier setup/action path, but because the job already hit the missing-action problem, that environment was not established correctly. The `set -u` shell option turns that into a hard failure.

### Recommended code change
If your intent is just to unblock CI quickly, do both:

1. **Fix the missing local action**
   - ensure `.github/actions/normalized-safe-checkout/action.yml` exists and is committed

2. **Harden the shell steps against unset `PYTHON_BIN`**
   - replace direct use of `"$PYTHON_BIN"` with a fallback

body:
## fix(process): use std_command for where/which to prevent CMD window flash

### Summary

Fixes visible CMD/PowerShell windows flashing on every YouTube download on Windows.

### Root cause

`detect_js_runtime()` used `std::process::Command::new()` directly to run `where` (locating JS runtimes), bypassing `std_command()` which sets `CREATE_NO_WINDOW` (`0x08000000`). Each invocation opened a visible console window.

### Fix

One-line change — replace `std::process::Command::new(finder)` with `crate::core::process::std_command(finder)`.

### Test plan

- [x] `cargo check` passes
- [x] No CMD windows flash during YouTube download on Windows

Closes #66

author: fbmcipher
body:
**Fixes #3887**

## Summary

Fixes the gesture menu getting permanently stuck in a visible state when rapidly swiping in the scroll zone then performing a gesture.

## Problem



When a user scrolls in the scroll zone and then immediately performs a gesture, iOS momentum scrolling continues generating scroll events during the gesture.

Logging shows this causes the `PanResponder` to repeatedly terminate and re-grant on each frame – `onPanResponderTerminate` and `onPanResponderGrant` cycle continuously as long as scroll events are firing.

This happens because React Native Web's responder system (`ResponderSystem.js`) terminates the current responder when a scroll event fires on a parent of the responder node.

Because the PanResponder is in a **terminated** state at `touchend` (once the user's finger leaves the screen after inputting a gesture), `onPanResponderRelease` never fires. This means `handleGestureEnd` never runs and the 400ms `gestureMenuTimeout` that opens the gesture menu is never cleared – leaving showGestureMenu permanently stuck as true.

## Fix

`onPanResponderTerminationRequest` now returns `false` when disableScroll is true (i.e., the user is in the gesture zone), preventing the scroll events from stealing the responder during an active gesture.

Fixes #335

## What

Adds `/vbw:report` — a self-diagnosis and bug reporting slash command. Users run it to collect diagnostic context and optionally file a GitHub issue with pre-populated environment data.

**Files modified:**
- `commands/report.md` (NEW) — slash command with 4-tier issue filing fallback
- `scripts/collect-diagnostics.sh` (NEW) — diagnostic collection with redaction
- `scripts/verify-vibe.sh` — CMD_COUNT 23→24
- `README.md` — `/vbw:report` in Supporting commands table, "25 commands"
- `marketplace.json` (root) — "25 commands"
- `.claude-plugin/marketplace.json` — "25 commands"
- `testing/verify-plugin-root-resolution.sh` — `report.md` in TARGET_COMMANDS

## Why

Users encountering VBW issues had no structured way to collect diagnostic context or file bug reports with the right environment details. This command automates that workflow with privacy-safe redaction and a multi-tier issue filing chain that works regardless of whether the user has `gh` CLI, GitHub MCP server, or neither.

## How

- **`commands/report.md`**: `disable-model-invocation: true` command with standard 6-step preamble. Parses `$ARGUMENTS` for `--file-issue` flag and problem description. Three-step flow: collect diagnostics → display report → offer next steps. The `--file-issue` path uses a 4-tier fallback chain:
  1. `gh` CLI (if installed and authenticated via `gh auth status`)
  2. GitHub MCP server (`mcp_github_issue_write`) if available in tool list
  3. Install `gh` (brew/apt), authenticate (`gh auth login --web`), then file
  4. Manual fallback URL (last resort)
  Uses heredoc temp files with `trap`-based cleanup for safe shell quoting.

- **`scripts/collect-diagnostics.sh`**: Collects VBW version, OS, Claude Code version, install method (with symlink resolution), plugin cache state, hook errors (last 20), session log (last 10), event log (last 20), metrics (last 10), redacted config.json (via `jq` with `walk()` polyfill for jq < 1.6), STATE.md, and doctor check summary. `redact()` masks `$HOME`, `$USER`, and token patterns (`sk-*` including `sk-ant-`/`sk-proj-`, `ghp_*`, `gho_*`, `github_pat_*`, `ghs_*`, `ghu_*`). Always exits 0. Uses `${HOME:-/tmp}` for `set -u` safety.

- **Supporting files**: Updated command count in `verify-vibe.sh`, `README.md`, both `marketplace.json` files. Added `report.md` to preamble verification targets.

5. **Accepts optional $ARGUMENTS** — satisfied by Parse Arguments section (L29-33)
6. **Readable structured format** — satisfied by fenced code block display (L44-48)

8. **Works without .vbw-planning/** — satisfied by `[ -f ... ]`/`[ -d ... ]` guards with fallback messages
9. **Single-line description** — satisfied: `description: Collect diagnostic context for bug reporting and optionally file a GitHub issue.`
10. **`set -u` minimum** — satisfied at L11
11. **Contract tests pass** — 367+492+18+63+44 PASS, 0 FAIL across all contract/lint checks

### Motivation
- Provide first-class support for running Gemma 4 locally via vLLM so the app can use a self-hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoint for AI assistance. 
- Allow each LLM provider to use a configurable base URL so non-standard or local endpoints (like a vLLM server) can be targeted from the app. 
- Permit providers that do not require API keys to be enabled and used without forcing a stored key.

### Description
- Added a new provider `VLLM_GEMMA4` to `LlmProvider` with a self-hosted default base URL and `requiresApiKey = false`, and added a default model `google/gemma-4-E4B-it`.

- Updated `LlmApiClient` to use `settings.baseUrl` (instead of the enum base) and added `callOpenAICompatible()` to send OpenAI-style `/chat/completions` requests to vLLM Gemma 4 using `Bearer EMPTY` when no API key is provided; routed `VLLM_GEMMA4` to that method.
- Extended the Settings UI (`fragment_settings.xml` and `SettingsFragment`) to add a `Base URL` input, provider-specific key hints and a vLLM info text, and added corresponding string resources; updated `README.md` with a quick-start note referencing the vLLM Gemma4 recipe.

author: snider
body:
🚨 **Severity:** CRITICAL
💡 **Vulnerability:** A hardcoded token `xrpc-9f8e7d6c5b4a` was discovered in `server-php/config/conf.d/wordpress.conf` allowing attackers to bypass XML-RPC blocks in Nginx simply by using `?token=xrpc-9f8e7d6c5b4a`.
🎯 **Impact:** Compromises security and allows trivial exploitation via simple query arguments. It also leaks access credentials into source control, enabling brute force and DDoS attacks commonly associated with WordPress XML-RPC.
🔧 **Fix:** Edited `server-php/config/conf.d/wordpress.conf` to replace the conditional logic for `/xmlrpc.php` with an unconditional `deny all;`, and disabled access and not-found logging. This entirely eliminates the hardcoded bypass token. Also recorded this as a critical learning in `.jules/sentinel.md`.
✅ **Verification:** Verified the code changes manually. Nginx config updates are correct and `.jules/sentinel.md` journal entry was created successfully.

Reasoning for strings is to show escaped strings, in case the content is not easy to differentiate. And also to easier differentiate strings from integer & booleans.

Reasoning for booleans is because `builtins.toString` has a [weird legacy behavior](https://nix.dev/manual/nix/2.23/language/builtins.html#builtins-toString) for booleans:
- `builtins.toString true == "1"`
- `builtins.toString false == ""`

Also: sheet sessions are ordered **earliest first** (chronological for that day). **Escape** or **backdrop tap** closes the sheet. --- ## Muscle-colored bars - Calendar **session bars** use **primary muscle** = exercise `categories[0]`, matched by exercise name (exact or case-insensitive) to the exercises library, with fallback to planned exercise name on the workout template. - **One primary muscle** across all sets in the session → **solid** bar in that muscle’s color. - **Exactly two primary muscles** → **50/50** horizontal split (equal flex, regardless of set counts). - **Three or more** → segments **proportional to set counts** per muscle. - **Multiple sessions on the same day**: **stacked** thin bars (one row per session). - Unknown / unmatched exercises use neutral gray (`#636366`). Colors: `src/lib/sessionMuscleBar.ts` (`MUSCLE_GROUP_COLORS`). --- ## Session detail back button - Header **back** uses **`navigate(-1)`** (previous route). body: ### Summary This PR adds SMS notifications to trainers at booking creation and payment confirmation, and enhances the TrainerDashboard booking cards to display richer client details including rating, location, session duration, and notes. ### Problem Trainers had no visibility into new bookings or payment completions via SMS, and the booking cards in the TrainerDashboard lacked key client information (rating, location, session duration, notes), making it harder for trainers to assess and manage their bookings at a glance. Additionally, payment completion was incorrectly reported as failed despite going through successfully. ### Solution - Integrated SMS notifications into the backend payment flow so trainers receive a confirmation SMS when a client's M-Pesa payment is confirmed. - Added a `getClientProfile` API utility and fetched client details per booking in the TrainerDashboard, enriching booking cards with client-specific data. - Fixed the payment status reporting to correctly reflect successful transactions. ### Key Changes - **`mpesa_helper.php`**: After a successful payment is recorded, fetches the trainer's phone number and sends a payment confirmation SMS via Onfonmedia using `sendSmsViaOnfonmedia`, with the result logged via `logSmsEvent`. - **`TrainerDashboard.tsx`**: - Added `clientDetails` state to store fetched client profiles keyed by client ID. - On bookings load, iterates over bookings and fetches each unique client's profile via `getClientProfile`. - Booking cards now display client star rating (with `Star` icon), area of residence (with `MapPin` icon), session duration (with `Clock` icon), and booking notes with a styled callout. - **`src/lib/api-service.ts`**: Added `getClientProfile(clientId)` function to query `user_profiles` by `user_id`. ---    --- To clone this PR locally use the [Github CLI](https://cli.github.com/) with command `gh pr checkout 260` You can tag me at @builderio for anything you want me to fix or change

author: hisandog
body:
## Summary

Lightweight type-safety and error-handling improvements across notify-hook scripts and sleep utility. All changes are strictly type-level or additive — **zero behavioral changes**.

## Changes (+37 / -11)

### 1. Replace `any` with concrete types (4 files)

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| **`log.ts`** | `logsDir: any` → `logsDir: string`, `event: any` → `event: Record<string, unknown>` |
| **`process-runner.ts`** | `chunk: any` → `chunk: Buffer`, `err: any` → `err: Error`, `code: any` → `code: number \| null` |
| **`utils.ts`** | `isTerminalPhase(phase: any)` → `phase: string` |
| **`log.ts`** | Extract `safeAppend` helper to replace inline `.catch(() => {})` with a documented no-op wrapper |

### 2. SleepSync fallback

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| **`sleep.ts`** | Wrap `Atomics.wait` in try/catch with busy-wait fallback for environments where `SharedArrayBuffer` is unavailable (e.g. `--no-shared-memory` flag) |

### 3. Visibility into daemon failures

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| **`notify-hook.ts`** | Replace `main().catch(() => process.exit(0))` (silent exit-0 discarding error) with error logging via `console.error` and `process.exitCode = 1` |

## Motivation

- The notify-hook scripts run as tmux daemon subprocesses; silenced errors make debugging production issues nearly impossible.
- Widespread `any` usage in these files means real type bugs (e.g. passing wrong argument types) slip through CI entirely.

body:
### Motivation
- The debug overlay was difficult to use on phones because repeated tap targets could trigger browser zoom and long effect panels scrolled off-screen, making parameter editing fiddly.
- The intent is to present fewer UI bits at once on small screens, provide a stable internal scroll region, and make it easy to switch between transport, effect selection/params, and render controls.

### Description
- Reworked the debug overlay markup to group controls into three sections (`Transport`, `Effects`, `Render`) with a tab row and an internal scroll container so a single panel can present sectioned content without page-level scrolling (updated `index.html`).
- Added responsive CSS: constrained panel `max-height`, internal scroll (`.debug-panel-scroll`), tab styles, larger tap targets, and `touch-action: manipulation` on action buttons to reduce accidental browser zoom (`src/style.css`).
- Added a typed section helper and constants (`DEBUG_PANEL_SECTIONS`, `getDebugPanelSection`) in `src/debug/debugPanel.ts` and wired mobile tab/section state handling and ARIA selection sync in `src/main.ts`, including auto-switch to the Effects section after selecting a forced effect.
- Updated docs to mention the new mobile tabbed behaviour and added a unit test exercising the new helper (`src/debug/debugPanel.test.ts`).

### Testing
- Ran the repository test suite with `npm test`; the run completed but one unrelated pre-existing test failed (`src/timeline/timelineAudioParams.test.ts`) and caused the overall suite to report failure (failure not caused by these changes).
- Ran the focused unit tests for the modified module with `npx vitest run src/debug/debugPanel.test.ts`, and the debug panel tests passed (10/10).

## What

## Why
The current output has redundant discovery messages, internal housekeeping lines that users don't need to see, and a verbose telemetry banner. Closes #275.

## How
- **Remove discovery noise**: Dropped `[claude-code] Discovered N JSONL files` console.warn and the "total session files discovered" block (with its `discoveryWarned` tracking variable). The spinner already shows "Discovering {provider} sessions..." — sufficient.

author: copilot
body:
Perspectives in the current model are shared state on a Case — no per-actor isolation, no draft/commit lifecycle, no access control. This makes independent perspective capture impossible: any actor can see (and be biased by) others' thinking before finalizing their own.

This PR introduces a blindness architecture that enforces epistemic separation at the data layer, not just UI.

### Domain model (`src/domain/types.ts`)
- `Perspective` type with `draft` → `committed` lifecycle, `actor_id` ownership, and structured `PerspectiveContent`
- `PerspectiveStatus` union, `PerspectiveContent` interface (observation, interpretation, counter-interpretation, uncertainty)

### Guards & factories (`src/domain/guards.ts`, `factories.ts`)
- Perspective-specific guards: status enum, content completeness at commit time, ID/timestamp validation
- `createPerspective()` — always produces a draft
- `commitPerspective()` — validates completeness, transitions to immutable committed state

### Access control (`src/domain/perspective-access.ts`)
Server-side enforcement, independent of any UI:

```ts
// Draft → owner only. Committed → anyone. No exceptions.
canReadPerspective(perspective, requestingActorId)
canWritePerspective(perspective, requestingActorId)

// Single choke-point: never leaks other actors' drafts
filterVisiblePerspectives(perspectives, requestingActorId)

// Comparison only when ≥2 committed — no partial reveals
getComparablePerspectives(perspectives, minRequired)
```

### Service layer (`apps/web/src/lib/services/perspective-service.ts`)
- Every function takes `requestingActorId` — no trust in caller
- CRUD + commit + comparison, all gated through access control
- Separate persistence store (`spannungsatlas-perspectives` key)

### Key invariants enforced
- Draft perspectives: no readability by others, no metadata leaks (count, existence, progress)
- Committed perspectives: visible but immutable
- Comparison mode: only activates with ≥2 committed perspectives

### Tests
84 new tests across 4 files (guards: 28, factories: 13, access control: 18, service: 25). All 328 tests pass.

author: jefflower
body:
## 问题

`rmcp` 1.3.0 将 `StreamableHttpClientTransportConfig` 标记为 `#[non_exhaustive]`，导致在定义 crate 外部无法使用结构体字面量构造（包括 `..Default::default()` 填充语法），编译报错：

```
error[E0639]: cannot create non-exhaustive struct using struct expression
```

## 修复

将结构体字面量替换为官方提供的 builder API：

```rust
// 修复前（编译失败）
StreamableHttpClientTransportConfig {
    uri: url.to_string(),
    headers: HeaderMap::new(),
    ..Default::default()
}

// 修复后
StreamableHttpClientTransportConfig::with_uri(url)
    .custom_headers(headers)
```

同时移除了不再使用的 `use std::sync::Arc` 导入。

## 测试

- `cargo build --workspace --lib` ✅ 编译通过
- `cargo test --workspace` ✅ 所有测试通过（1744+）

author: hubeiqiao
body:
## Summary
- **Scroll morph fisheye**: Cards scale based on Gaussian proximity to viewport center, creating a subtle depth effect while scrolling
- **Pinch-to-zoom**: CSS zoom on container via Ctrl+wheel, Cmd+/-/0 keyboard shortcuts, and touch pinch gestures. Zoom level persists in localStorage with floating percentage badge
- **Mobile UX**: Labeled pill chip filters with horizontal scroll + edge fade gradient. Compact icon-only theme/lang toggles inline with title. Both scroll morph and zoom disabled on mobile (<640px)

## Key design decisions
- **CSS `zoom` for pinch zoom** (not `transform: scale()`) — scale doesn't affect layout boxes, causing card overlap in grids
- **CSS `translate` for fade-up animation** (not `transform: translateY()`) — animation-fill-mode:both permanently overrides transform, blocking the morph scale
- **Desktop only** — scroll morph and zoom disabled on mobile where viewport is already constrained
- **Gaussian falloff** (σ = 0.4 × viewport height) for natural fisheye proximity curve

## Test plan
- [ ] Desktop: scroll page, verify cards near center scale to ~1x and distant cards scale down to ~0.92x
- [ ] Desktop: Ctrl+scroll wheel zooms in/out, floating badge appears at cursor
- [ ] Desktop: Cmd/Ctrl + +/-/0 keyboard shortcuts work
- [ ] Desktop: zoom persists across page reloads (localStorage)
- [ ] Mobile (375px): no scroll morph or zoom effects applied
- [ ] Mobile: pill chip filters scroll horizontally with edge fade
- [ ] Mobile: theme toggle shows icons only, inline with title

body:
## Summary
- **Scroll morph fisheye**: Cards scale based on Gaussian proximity to viewport center, creating a subtle depth effect while scrolling
- **Pinch-to-zoom**: CSS zoom on container via Ctrl+wheel, Cmd+/-/0 keyboard shortcuts, and touch pinch gestures. Zoom level persists in localStorage with floating percentage badge
- **Mobile UX**: Labeled pill chip filters with horizontal scroll + edge fade gradient. Compact icon-only theme/lang toggles inline with title. Both scroll morph and zoom disabled on mobile (<640px)

## Key design decisions
- **CSS `zoom` for pinch zoom** (not `transform: scale()`) — scale doesn't affect layout boxes, causing card overlap in grids
- **CSS `translate` for fade-up animation** (not `transform: translateY()`) — animation-fill-mode:both permanently overrides transform, blocking the morph scale
- **Desktop only** — scroll morph and zoom disabled on mobile where viewport is already constrained
- **Gaussian falloff** (σ = 0.4 × viewport height) for natural fisheye proximity curve

## Test plan

author: dimotai
body:
# fix: catch NPE in EnchantmentSlotTracker when players transfer between worlds

## Problem

`EnchantmentSlotTracker` produces massive log spam (~20 exceptions/sec per affected player) when any player transfers from the `default` world to a dungeon instance or other world.

The tracker runs every 50ms via `HytaleServer.SCHEDULED_EXECUTOR.scheduleAtFixedRate()`. Each tick it iterates all worlds, queues a lambda to each world thread via `world.execute()`, and calls `checkPlayerSlot()` for every `PlayerRef`. When a player transfers between worlds, their entity is removed from the origin world's `Store`, setting the internal `ArchetypeChunk` to `null`. However, the queued lambda still iterates the stale `PlayerRef` on the next tick.

The existing validity guards on lines 96 and 104 (`playerRef.isValid()`, `ref.isValid()`) pass because the ref hasn't been formally invalidated yet — but by the time `Store.getComponent()` executes on line 108, `Store.__internal_getComponent()` dereferences the null `ArchetypeChunk` and throws `NullPointerException`. This is a TOCTOU (time-of-check-to-time-of-use) race inherent to the queued execution model.

The exception is caught by the engine's task queue runner and logged as `[World|default] Failed to run task!` with a full stack trace, but the tracker re-fires on the next tick, hitting the same stale ref again. On a server with active dungeon instances, this produces 1,000+ exceptions per minute and floods the console.

### Stack trace

```
java.lang.NullPointerException: Cannot invoke "ArchetypeChunk.getComponent(int, ComponentType)" because "archetypeChunk" is null
    at Store.__internal_getComponent(Store.java:1226)
    at Store.getComponent(Store.java:1214)
    at EnchantmentSlotTracker.checkPlayerSlot(EnchantmentSlotTracker.java:108)
    at EnchantmentSlotTracker.lambda$run$0(EnchantmentSlotTracker.java:69)
    at World.consumeTaskQueue(World.java:967)
    at World.tick(World.java:458)
    at TickingThread.run(TickingThread.java:95)
```

## Fix

Wrap the `checkPlayerSlot()` call inside the `world.execute()` lambda with a try-catch for `NullPointerException`. On catch, clean up the stale tracking data (`lastSlotMap`) for that player UUID.

The catch is placed at the call site in the lambda rather than inside `checkPlayerSlot()` because no amount of pre-checking can prevent the race — the entity can be removed between any validity check and the subsequent component access. This cleanly handles all current and future NPE paths from the same root cause.

## Impact

- Eliminates ~20 exception stack traces per second per player in a dungeon instance
- No behavioral change for players who remain in their world — the normal `checkPlayerSlot` path is unaffected
- Stale tracking data is cleaned up on first failure rather than waiting for the disconnect cleanup pass

## Summary

Makes the Copilot review cycle fully autonomous — open a PR, walk away, come back when it's ready to merge.

### Changes

- **CI gate between rounds**: After Copilot pushes fixes, `waitForCi()` polls check runs and blocks until CI passes before dispatching the next review round. Prevents wasting review rounds on broken code.
- **CI gate + ready-to-merge signal**: When review passes clean, waits for CI green, then adds `ready-to-merge` label and posts a definitive status comment.
- **Auto-merge option**: New `auto_merge` workflow input (default: false). When true, enables `gh pr merge --auto --squash` after clean review + green CI.
- **Fix issue lifecycle**: Closes stale fix issues when review passes clean. Deduplicates fix issues across rounds (closes old before creating new). Safety-net workflow (`close-copilot-fix-issues.yml`) closes any remaining when PR merges.
- **Smoke test fix**: Updated stale data markers to use regex patterns instead of hardcoded values that break on daily pipeline runs.

### New flow

```
PR opened → Review → Comments?
  Yes → Close old fix issues → Create fix issue (assign Copilot)
      → Wait for fixes → Wait for CI green → Dispatch next round
  No  → Close fix issues → Wait for CI green
      → Add "ready-to-merge" label + post summary
      → (if auto_merge) enable auto-merge
```

### Files changed

| File | What |
|---|---|
| `scripts/copilot-review-cycle.ts` | Added `waitForCi()`, `closeFixIssues()`, `addLabel()`, `enableAutoMerge()`, CI gates, auto-merge support |
| `.github/workflows/copilot-review-cycle.yml` | Added `auto_merge` input, `AUTO_MERGE` env var |
| `.github/workflows/close-copilot-fix-issues.yml` | New — safety-net to close fix issues on PR merge |
| `.github/workflows/post-deploy-smoke.yml` | Regex patterns for data markers, HTTP status validation, shared fetch helper |

## Test plan

### Motivation

- Migrate the Script tab to a canonical ProseMirror-style `scriptDocument` model and unify breakdown tags and Visualize shot links onto a structured `scriptAnnotations` substrate while preserving existing workflows and backwards compatibility.
- Provide a safe rollout path with a legacy ScriptTab fallback governed by a runtime flag so the new editor can be enabled incrementally without breaking historical projects.

### Description

- Introduces a ProseMirror compatibility bridge and normalization utilities in `src/features/scriptDocument/legacyBridge.js` and exposes `normalizeScriptDocumentState`, `convertProseMirrorDocumentToLegacyCompatibility`, and related helpers to convert between legacy `scriptScenes` and the canonical `scriptDocument` payload.
- Adds a structured annotation model and helpers in `src/features/scriptDocument/breakdownAnnotations.js` including kinds `breakdown_annotation`, `shot_link_annotation`, and `comment_annotation`, plus functions to `upsertShotLinkAnnotation`, `removeShotLinkAnnotationByShotId`, migrate legacy ranges, and derive per-scene indexes and breakdown lists.
- Implements a debounced derivation pipeline in `src/features/scriptDocument/derivationPipeline.js` that builds adapter-compatible outputs (`scriptScenes`, `breakdownAggregates`, `breakdownLists`, `shotLinkIndexBySceneId`) from `scriptDocument` and `scriptAnnotations` while keeping legacy fallbacks.
- Adds a paginated document surface `ScriptDocumentPaginationSurface.jsx` and pagination logic in `scriptPagination.js` to render / edit the canonical document, and wires a `ScriptTabLegacy` wrapper with a runtime flag in `src/components/ScriptTab.jsx` and `src/config/runtimeConfig.js` (`VITE_ENABLE_LEGACY_SCRIPT_TAB`) to control the rollout.
- Updates the application store (`src/store.js`) to persist `scriptDocument`, `scriptAnnotations`, derivation state and cache, to provide `updateScriptDocumentLive`, `deriveScriptDocumentNow`, `flushScriptDocumentDerivation`, and annotation CRUD actions, and to write shot-link annotations from `linkShotToScene` while preserving legacy shot fields for compatibility.
- Adds many docs under `docs/` describing the phased migration and compatibility guardrails and scaffolds comment entities (data-only) without enabling comment UI.

### Testing

- Added unit tests for annotation logic in `breakdownAnnotations.test.mjs` which exercise add/remove, migration, upsert/remove shot-link behavior, and comment-annotation rails, and these tests passed.
- Added unit tests for the derivation pipeline in `derivationPipeline.test.mjs` covering aggregates, shot-index derivation, and the debouncer semantics, and these tests passed.
- Added unit tests for the ProseMirror legacy bridge in `legacyBridge.test.mjs` covering round-trip conversions, normalization, and legacy migrations, and these tests passed.
- Added unit tests for pagination in `scriptPagination.test.mjs` to validate deterministic pagination and scene-break behavior, and these tests passed.

body:
## Summary

- Adds `apps/papillon-extension/src/db/` — a native IndexedDB persistence layer for the Papillon Chrome extension
- `schema.ts`: domain types (`Session`, `Mandate`, `Credential`, `Episode`) plus `createSchema()` that creates 4 object stores with appropriate indexes on first open
- `db.ts`: `PapDB` class with `static open(factory?)`, `saveSession`, `getSession`, `listActiveSessions`, `updateSessionStatus`, `saveMandate`, `getMandatesBySession`, `saveCredential`, `getCredentialsBySubject`, `recordEpisode`, `getEpisodesBySession`, and `purgeExpired`
- `index.ts`: barrel re-exports
- `db.test.ts`: 27 vitest tests using `fake-indexeddb` with a fresh `IDBFactory` per test for full isolation
- `vitest.config.ts`: minimal vitest configuration

## Design decisions

- **No external library** — plain `IDBRequest`/`IDBTransaction` wrappers (`requestToPromise`, `transactionComplete`)
- **Injectable `IDBFactory`** — `PapDB.open(factory?)` accepts a custom factory so tests use `fake-indexeddb` without patching globals
- **Progressive decay** — `SessionStatus` union covers all five states (Active → Degraded → ReadOnly → Suspended → Closed) per spec
- **Property references only** — `Episode.outcome` stores references, never raw credential values
- **`expires_at` is nullable on `Credential`** — non-expiring credentials are a valid first-class case

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` in `apps/papillon-extension/` — all 27 tests pass
- [x] `npx tsc --noEmit` — zero TypeScript errors
- [ ] Manual: load extension in Chrome, open handshake, verify sessions appear in DevTools → Application → IndexedDB → pap_extension

### Motivation

author: jb-git72
body:
## Summary

Tests whether chaining crossover + mutation in the same generation produces better landing pages than plain crossover alone. Three approaches tested on 4 Farm Thru LPs (LP-A, LP-F, LP-D, LP-P), 2 candidates each = 24 scored variants.

- **Approach A (baseline):** Plain crossover with current hook — 1 API call
- **Approach B (single-call combo):** Crossover with a mutated hook in the same prompt — 1 API call
- **Approach C (two-call chain):** Crossover first, then mutate the result with a new hook — 2 API calls

## Results

```
                      Avg Score  Best Score    Win Rate     N
-------------------------------------------------------------
Approach A (Plain crossover  ):    0.685       0.744         75%     8
Approach B (Single-call combo):    0.608       0.731          0%     8
Approach C (Two-call chain   ):    0.673       0.720         25%     8
```

**Plain crossover (A) wins** — chaining does not help. Hook mutation during crossover (B) actively hurts scores (-11% vs baseline). The two-call chain (C) is slightly better than B but still underperforms plain crossover by -1.8%.

### Per-LP breakdown

| LP | Current | A avg | B avg | C avg | Winner |
|----|---------|-------|-------|-------|--------|
| LP-A | 0.582 | 0.629 | 0.591 | **0.661** | C |
| LP-F | 0.658 | 0.715 | **0.726** | 0.718 | B* |
| LP-D | 0.733 | **0.683** | 0.518 | 0.643 | A |
| LP-P | 0.647 | **0.715** | 0.598 | 0.670 | A |

*LP-F is the only case where B beats A — and only by +0.011.

### Key observations
- Hook mutation during crossover confuses the LLM — it tries to do too many things at once and produces worse copy
- The "exclusivity" hook was particularly damaging for LP-D (B scored 0.518 vs A's 0.683)
- Chain step 1 sometimes produces excellent intermediates (LP-A C-2 step 1 hit 0.771) but the mutation step consistently degrades them
- LP-P C-1 step 1 got a 0.000 (rules gate fail) but step 2 recovered to 0.644 — mutation can rescue bad crossovers

### Recommendation
Keep crossover and mutation as independent operations in the evolutionary strategy. No code changes needed.

## Test plan
- [x] Script runs end-to-end on 4 LPs with all 3 approaches
- [x] Results captured in `results/chained-evolution-results.txt`
- [x] 24 variants scored with LLM scoring enabled
- [ ] Review data before deciding on any engine changes

author: w0wl0lxd
body:
## Summary

- **Add Kilo Code agent** — new `--agent kilo` option using `kilo serve` + SSE streaming. Kilo is a fork of OpenCode with the same API, so `KiloAgent` is a 10-line subclass of the extracted `ServeBasedAgent` base class (883 → 10 lines, -873 lines of duplication).
- **Fix Codex backpressure hang** — replaced event-based stdout parsing with async `for await...of` iteration and `stderr.resume()` to prevent pipe-buffer deadlock. Added 60s startup timeout to detect MCP-related hangs early.
- **Extract `ServeBasedAgent` base class** — shared serve-mode logic between OpenCode and Kilo agents with protected override points for agent-specific names, error messages, and debug prefixes.

## Memory & reliability fixes (from code review)

| Issue | Fix |
|-------|-----|
| Unbounded stderr buffer growth | Cap at 64KB in codex.ts and stream-utils.ts |
| Duplicate stderr listeners | Remove no-op listener from consumeJSONLStream, use `stderr.resume()` |
| Orphaned async iterator on error | Call `stdout.destroy()` in error handler before rejecting |
| Listener leaks on close/error | Use `child.once()` instead of `child.on()`; clean up stderr handlers |
| Double-reject in abort handler | Guard with `settled` flag |
| O(M²N) token accumulation | Convert to O(1) incremental delta tracking |
| `AbortSignal.timeout` timer leak | Wrap in `AbortController` with `clearTimeout` on success |
| `new Headers()` allocation per request | Use plain `Record<string, string>` object |
| SSE `split/filter/map` intermediate arrays | Replace with single `for...of` loop |
| Redundant server check | Remove duplicate check in ensureServer |
| `response.text()` losing error context | Guard with try/catch in request method |

## Files changed (13 files, +983 / -241)

- `src/core/agents/kilo.ts` (new) — 10-line KiloAgent subclass
- `src/core/agents/kilo.test.ts` (new) — 7 tests covering spawn, Windows shell, tokens, error, close
- `src/core/agents/opencode.ts` — extracted ServeBasedAgent base class, O(1) token tracking, AbortController timeout, plain object headers, zero-allocation SSE parser
- `src/core/agents/codex.ts` — async stream handling, 60s startup timeout, capped stderr buffer, child.once() listeners
- `src/core/agents/codex.test.ts` — updated for async pattern + stderr content verification
- `src/core/agents/stream-utils.ts` — consumeJSONLStream with error propagation, double-reject guard, cleanup functions
- `src/core/agents/factory.ts` — added kilo case

- `src/core/config.ts` — added kilo to AgentName union

- `README.md` — documented Kilo in agents table

All 287 tests pass, lint clean, build 113KB.

| Unbounded stderr buffer growth | Cap at 64KB in codex.ts and stream-utils.ts |
| Duplicate stderr listeners | Remove no-op listener from consumeJSONLStream, use `stderr.resume()` |
| Orphaned async iterator on error | Call `stdout.destroy()` in error handler before rejecting |
| Listener leaks on close/error | Use `child.once()` instead of `child.on()`; clean up stderr handlers |
| Double-reject in abort handler | Guard with `settled` flag |
| O(M²N) token accumulation | Convert to O(1) incremental delta tracking |
| `AbortSignal.timeout` timer leak | Wrap in `AbortController` with `clearTimeout` on success |
| `new Headers()` allocation per request | Use plain `Record<string, string>` object |
| SSE `split/filter/map` intermediate arrays | Replace with single `for...of` loop |
| Redundant server check | Remove duplicate check in ensureServer |
| `response.text()` losing error context | Guard with try/catch in request method |

- `src/core/agents/kilo.ts` (new) — 10-line KiloAgent subclass
- `src/core/agents/kilo.test.ts` (new) — 7 tests covering spawn, Windows shell, tokens, error, close
- `src/core/agents/opencode.ts` — extracted ServeBasedAgent base class, O(1) token tracking, AbortController timeout, plain object headers, zero-allocation SSE parser
- `src/core/agents/codex.ts` — async stream handling, 60s startup timeout, capped stderr buffer, child.once() listeners
- `src/core/agents/codex.test.ts` — updated for async pattern + stderr content verification
- `src/core/agents/stream-utils.ts` — consumeJSONLStream with error propagation, double-reject guard, cleanup functions

Bootstraps the multi-agent coordination layer for this submodule repo. Agents connect to a local Redis server, broadcast heartbeats/status, maintain a live peer registry, and enforce socialization on every user interaction. A manager agent monitors the team and guards project alignment.

## New classes

- **`ExtrovertAgent`** (`extrovert_agent.py`) — inherits `AgentBase`; adds peer registry, socialization routine (heartbeat → status → project re-eval → peer ACK → team report), and mandatory `=== Team Status ===` block on every user interaction. Status broadcast every 60s and after every 3 actions.
- **`LonelyManager`** (`lonely_manager.py`) — inherits `ExtrovertAgent`; heartbeat monitor checks every 5s per agent, fires `LOST` alert after 5 missed beats via configurable `alert_callback`, requests status from all agents every 60s, sends realignment nudges to agents silent >2 min, persists full team state to Redis hashes (`lonely_manager:team_state:<agent_id>`) for external query.

```python
manager = LonelyManager(
    agent_id="lonely_manager",
    alert_callback=lambda alert: notify_user(alert["message"]),
    todo_path="TODO.md",
    roadmap_path="roadmap.md",
)
manager.start()

# Query live team snapshot from Redis (no pub/sub required)
snapshot = manager.get_redis_team_snapshot()
```

- **`redis.conf`** — local Redis config (127.0.0.1:6379, 64 MB cap, persistence off, auth guidance inline)
- **`requirements.txt`** — `redis>=5.0.0`
- **`__init__.py`** — package init exporting all five public classes

author: yukieiji
body:
The existing `exrOptionsPromise` and `auOptionsPromise` were only providing "all-or-nothing" access to the configuration data. To support more efficient rendering and granular UI updates (especially with React 19's `use()` hook), these have been decomposed.

Changes:
1.  **Granular Caching:** Introduced `Map<number, Promise<ExRTabDto>>` and `Map<string, Promise<AuOptionCategoryDto>>` to store promises for individual tabs and categories.
2.  **New Getters:** 
    - `getExrTabOptions(tabId)`: Retrieves a specific tab's promise.
    - `getAuCategoryOptions(categoryName)`: Retrieves a specific category's promise (using the translated title).
3.  **Automatic Pre-population:** The main fetch functions (`getExrOptions` and `getAuOptions`) now populate these granular caches once the data is received. This ensures that any subsequent requests for a specific tab or category resolve immediately.
4.  **Promise Stability:** Granular getters return the same Promise instance for repeated calls to the same ID/name before the main fetch completes, preventing redundant fetching logic and meeting React 19 requirements.
5.  **Testing:** A new test file `tests/api-decomposition.test.ts` was added to verify:
    - Triggering main fetch from granular getters.
    - Returning the same promise instance.
    - Pre-population behavior.
    - Cache reset behavior.

These changes provide the infrastructure for optimizing component rendering by allowing components to suspend only on the specific data they require.

author: hariprrasadias-collab
body:
🚨 Severity: CRITICAL
💡 Vulnerability: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerabilities found when fetching URLs via `requests.get()` without validation in `neural_lace_service.py` and `upsc_summarizer.py`.
🎯 Impact: Attackers could supply malicious URLs to the AI summarizer or ingestion endpoints, causing the backend to make unauthorized requests to internal infrastructure (e.g. `localhost:5000`, AWS metadata endpoint `169.254.169.254`, or other private subnets), potentially leaking sensitive configuration or credentials.
🔧 Fix: Created a new security utility `safe_fetch_url` in `backend/app/utils/security.py` that resolves hostnames to IPs and explicitly blocks requests to private, loopback, multicast, and unspecified addresses before performing the HTTP GET request. Updated `neural_lace_service` and `upsc_summarizer` to use this secure implementation instead of native `requests`.
✅ Verification: Tested the new `is_safe_ip` utility independently against local, internal, and external IP patterns. Verified `ruff` linting passes for the modified files.

Custom Tidal-focused stream changes could not be imported end-to-end because playback quality modes and external HiFi stream resolution were not wired through settings, resolver, and playback services.

**💡 What:** Removed intermediate `Vec` allocations during string splitting in `session.rs` and replaced loop-based collection with `vec!` macros for constant-sized arrays in `offline.rs`.

This PR avoids running the nightly bug finder, code architect, and security review workflows when `main` has had no new commits in the last 24 hours. It keeps manual dispatches unchanged while cutting unnecessary long-running agent work on idle days.

author: copilot
body:
Extends AIOSCPU with a fixed self kernel, a switchable environment kernel, and a debuggable loop engine — all layered on top of the existing system without replacing or breaking it.

## Self Kernel (`/usr/lib/aios/self-kernel/`)
- **`identity.js`** — stable wrapper over `etc/aios/identity.json`; `getIdentity()`, `getKernelId()`, `getVersion()`, `getBuildId()`, `reload()`
- **`boot.js`** — lifecycle bridge; `bootSelfKernel()`, `startCoreServices()`, `attachLoopEngine(kernel, svcMgr, router, loopCtrl)`
- **`process-model.js`** / **`services.js`** — thin proxies over the existing process model and service manager with stable, named APIs
- **`loop-core.js`** — environment-agnostic loop state machine; `initLoop()`, `runLoopStep()`, `shutdownLoop()`

## Environment Kernel (`/usr/lib/aios/env-kernel/`)
- **`mode.js`** — selects `self` vs `mirror` mode; respects `AIOS_MODE` env var and `/aios-root` presence; runtime `switchMode()`
- **`fs-adapter.js`** — maps logical AIOS paths to real host paths per mode (`/home → /host-home` in mirror, `/ → /aios-root` in self)
- **`host-info.js`** — detects Termux / Android / Linux / macOS / Windows; `getPlatform()`, `getHostSummary()`

## Loop Engine (`/usr/lib/aios/loop/`)
- **`engine.js`** — ordered node pipeline `me → host → aios → cpu → ai → os → world`; supports hot-reload of individual nodes via `reloadNode(name)` / `reloadAllNodes()`
- **`context.js`** — immutable, frozen context object flowing through each cycle
- **`logger.js`** — per-hop logging at `silent` / `normal` / `verbose` levels
- **`control.js`** — shell-facing surface: `start()`, `stop()`, `step()`, `status()`
- **7 loop nodes** — each attaches read-only data (host info, kernel state, process list, AI summary, VFS state, world diagnostics) to the context; no destructive side-effects

## Shell Commands
New commands wired through the existing router in `boot/bootstrap.js`:

| Command | Behaviour |
|---|---|
| `loop start` | Start the ticking loop engine |
| `loop stop` | Stop it |
| `loop status` | Print mode, last node, cycle count, tick interval |
| `loop step` | Run one cycle; print context summary |
| `kernel mode` | Print `host_mode` and kernel ID |
| `kernel switch self` | Switch to self mode (requires `/aios-root`) |
| `kernel switch mirror` | Switch to mirror mode |

The backup brain in `personality-kernel.js` is extended with matching rules so the AI layer can dispatch these commands via natural language.

All existing boot behaviour, commands, and module wiring in `bootstrap.js` are untouched.

## Summary

- **ClickHouse QBit vector storage**: Enterprise-tier alternative to pgvector that stores embeddings in ClickHouse QBit columns (bit-plane encoding) partitioned by `org_id` — no in-memory HNSW index needed, tunable precision at query time
- **Parallel hybrid retrieval**: New `HybridRetrievalService` runs BM25 (PostgreSQL/ParadeDB) and QBit vector search (ClickHouse) in parallel goroutines, fusing results with Reciprocal Rank Fusion (k=60)
- **Graceful fallback**: When ClickHouse is unavailable or not configured, the system transparently falls back to pgvector — zero disruption to existing deployments

### New files
- `internal/db/clickhouse.go` — ClickHouse connection with LZ4 compression
- `internal/repository/clickhouse_embedding.go` — Store, search (cosine distance), batch insert, delete by KB/chunk, count by org
- `internal/service/hybrid_retrieval.go` — Parallel BM25 + vector search with RRF fusion and chunk content enrichment
- `internal/model/clickhouse.go` — `VectorBackend` type, `ClickHouseEmbedding`, `ClickHouseSearchResult`
- `deploy/clickhouse/init.sql` — DDL with QBit index

| Env var | Default | Description |

## Summary

When a `bead_cancelled` event is processed, agents hooked to that bead in `working` or `stalled` status were left running until the 90-second heartbeat timeout detected them as stale. N/A

author: jetd1
body:
## Motivation

Add support for Anthropic's thinking/reasoning tokens API in the `/v1/messages` endpoint, enabling Claude Code and other Anthropic-compatible clients to use reasoning models (GLM-5, DeepSeek-V3, etc.) with thinking support.

This PR extends PR #19334 by adding support for Claude 4.6+ adaptive thinking format (`thinking: {type: "adaptive"}`) and `output_config.effort` parameter.

## Modifications

### protocol.py
- Add `AnthropicThinkingParam` class supporting `"enabled"`, `"disabled"`, and `"adaptive"` types
- Add `AnthropicOutputConfig` class with `effort` parameter (`"low"`, `"medium"`, `"high"`, `"max"`)
- Add `thinking` and `output_config` fields to `AnthropicMessagesRequest`
- Add `"thinking_delta"` type to `AnthropicDelta`

### serving.py
- Wire `thinking` parameter to chat request (`separate_reasoning`, `stream_reasoning`, `enable_thinking`)
- Map `"adaptive"` type to enabled thinking (model controls reasoning depth internally)
- Accept `output_config.effort` as no-op (ensures Claude Code compatibility)
- Convert `reasoning_content` to Anthropic `thinking` content blocks in streaming responses
- Convert `reasoning_content` to Anthropic `thinking` content blocks in non-streaming responses

## Compatibility

| Client Request | Behavior |
|----------------|----------|
| `thinking: {type: "enabled"}` | Enables thinking, outputs thinking blocks |
| `thinking: {type: "disabled"}` | Disables thinking |
| `thinking: {type: "adaptive"}` | Enables thinking (model decides depth) |
| `output_config: {effort: "high"}` | Accepted, no-op (model controls depth) |

## Testing

Tested with:
- GLM-5 via Claude Code (adaptive thinking format)
- Streaming and non-streaming responses
- Tool calling with thinking enabled

Closes #19257

### Motivation
- Avoid updating `chunkBlocks` on every individual block add/remove and prevent generated or permanent block operations from marking chunks as modified.
- Introduce a mechanism to batch and apply block changes per chunk to improve performance and correctness when generating/unloading chunks.

### Description
- Added `dirtyChunks` and `chunkBlockDiffs` to `worldState` to track per-chunk adds/removes as diffs and a set of dirty chunk keys in `src/state.js`.
- Introduced `markChunkDirtyWithDelta` and `applyDirtyChunks` to record add/remove deltas and apply them to `chunkBlocks` in `src/blocks.js` and `src/worldgen.js` respectively.
- Extended `addBlock` and `removeBlock` to accept a `trackDirty` flag and call the new delta tracker when appropriate, and updated chunk generation and unloading paths to pass `trackDirty: false` for generated/permanent operations to avoid spurious dirtiness.
- Updated chunk generation (`generateChunk`), unloading (`unloadChunk`), and update loop (`updateChunks`) to use the new deferred application of diffs so `chunkBlocks` is updated in a single pass via `applyDirtyChunks`.
